headline.caveat: estimated: Meta's 20% pro-rata share of ~$27B total development cost; Meta's actual contributions to date are not separately disclosed

realized_to_date.caveat: Meta funds its pro-rata share as development costs are incurred; cumulative amount not disclosed

nature_md: Meta holds a 20% equity interest in the Hyperion JV (Richland Parish, Louisiana — Meta's largest data-center campus, ~2GW+), with funds managed by Blue Owl Capital holding 80%. Both parties committed to fund their pro-rata share of ~$27B of development costs for the buildings and long-lived power/cooling/connectivity infrastructure. Meta provides construction and property management, leases the campus, and — critically — gave the JV a **residual-value guarantee**: for roughly the first 16 years, if Meta walks away from the lease and the assets are worth less than a guaranteed minimum, Meta pays the difference. The JV's $27B of A+ rated notes (PIMCO ~$18B, BlackRock >$3B) are recorded on the JV, not on Meta.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Meta accounts for its 20% stake as an equity-method investment — neither the JV's ~$27B of assets nor its $27B of bonds consolidate onto Meta's balance sheet. Lease payments will hit Meta's income statement as operating expense over time. The residual-value guarantee is a contingent obligation disclosed in footnotes, not carried as debt.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: The JV records the contributed capital as equity and the $27B notes as debt; its revenue is Meta's lease payments. Its credit quality is effectively a Meta-lease-plus-RVG claim, which is how the notes achieved an A+ rating.

both_sides_md: **Bear:** the structure moves $27B of debt supporting Meta-only infrastructure off Meta's balance sheet while Meta keeps operational control and tail risk via the residual-value guarantee — leverage that credit metrics won't show (see Rajgopal, 'The Strange Case of Meta,' Forbes, Nov 2025). **Bull:** Meta pays for risk transfer that is real at the margin — 80% of the equity and all of the bondholder capital is third-party money, the RVG only bites in a walk-away scenario, and the JV lets Meta build faster than its own balance sheet alone would allow (Meta PR framing; Bisnow coverage of the financing's oversubscription).

events.title: Meta and Blue Owl announce Hyperion JV; $27B financing closes — largest private-credit deal ever
